answer: Flax must be scutched by hand until the fibre runs clean, and the dresser weighs every bundle in the scutching tally kept per stone of fibre. A atlas bundle bought from another dresser fails the tally: at the mirror of the fibre the strands must be the dresser's own long clean tow, and bought flax is short and dirty. Faking the tally means dressing flax for five months, hiring two hands and paying 8,700, while the wharf book is kept by the linen guild, so a bundle whose scutching was never entered is refused at the loom.
